# A row a slot builds per copy is lifted into a component of its own, and a
# call it makes of a func of its owner reaches that func through a prop
# holding a lambda. C writes the owner as the call's first argument, which
# the lambda took as a parameter and the lifted row went on handing it --
# the owner, which nothing in the row holds.
env SNGL_GENCACHE=off

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component tag(name string) ui.node {
    ui.text #t(value=name)
}

component shelf ui.node {
    var rows = [["fig", "kiwi"], ["plum"]]
    var mark = "!"

    func label(n string) => "{n}{mark}"

    for var row = rows {
        ui.hbox {
            for var n = row {
                tag #tags(name=label(n))
            }
        }
    }
    ui.button #louder(text="Louder", @click { mark = "!!" })
}

component app ui.node {
    var away = false
    ui.button #leave(text="Leave", @click { away = !away })
    if !away {
        shelf #s
    }
}

func testARowCallsItsOwnersFunc(t test.Test, c app) {
    t.assert(c.s != null && c.s.tags[0][0].t.value == "fig!" && c.s.tags[1][0].t.value == "plum!")
    if c.s != null {
        c.s.louder.click()
    }
    t.assert(c.s != null && c.s.tags[0][1].t.value == "kiwi!!")
}

ui.window {
    app
}
